\begin{Theorem}[Verified correspondence and switching decision]
\label{thm:formal_switching}
Let $w_1,w_2,w_3\in\mathcal B$, put $f_i=\nu(w_i)$, and suppose
$f_1f_2<0$. Define $\rho,s,p_i,h,G,L,R$ as in
\eqref{M-eq:switch_exact_sides}--\eqref{M-eq:switch_scaled_gap}.
Every intermediate arithmetic result in the evaluation of
$\mathcal E_{64}$ is finite, and every divisor is positive. Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
 \widehat G:=\nu\bigl(\mathcal E_{64}(w_1,w_2,w_3)\bigr)
   =\mathcal E_{\rm rn}(f_1,f_2,f_3),\qquad
 |\widehat G-G|\le25\epsilon.
 \label{eq:formal_complete_error}
\end{equation}
The executable comparisons with the binary64 representations of
$2^{-48}$ and $-2^{-48}$ consequently satisfy
\[
 \widehat G>2^{-48}\ \Longrightarrow\ L<R,
 \qquad
 \widehat G<-2^{-48}\ \Longrightarrow\ R<L.
\]
They select the respective branches whenever $G>57\epsilon$ or
$G<-57\epsilon$.
\end{Theorem}

\begin{proof}
The hypothesis implies that the endpoint magnitudes and their maximum
are positive. It follows that $s>0$, $0<\rho\le1$ and $|p_i|\le1$.
The normalized endpoint values have opposite signs. Their rounded
values retain the weak sign inequalities even if one of them becomes
zero, and hence $|\widehat p_1+\widehat p_2|\le1$.

Monotonicity of $\operatorname{rn}$ gives the intervals for the
computed factor stated in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{M-thm:switch_scaled_error}, as well as
$|\widehat h|\le1/2$. The exact results to which rounding is applied
all belong to $[-2,2]$. The endpoint maximum and $s$ are positive,
$\widehat b\ge1$, and the remaining divisor is $2$.
These facts are established before using
\eqref{eq:formal_operation_correspondence}.

Apply that relation successively to the arithmetic subexpressions.
For the initial input expressions, equality of real values is the
definition of $f_i$. If equality has already been established for the
operands of an operation, its range bound and, where needed, its
positive divisor allow \eqref{eq:formal_operation_correspondence} to
be applied. The new representation is finite and its value agrees
with the corresponding rounded real expression. Induction over the
expression therefore proves the equality in
\eqref{eq:formal_complete_error} and finiteness of all intermediate
results.

Lemma~\ref{lem:formal_rounding_error} now supplies each local absolute
error bound, and Lemma~\ref{lem:formal_factor_halving} supplies the
exact first halving. The formal real-arithmetic argument then derives
the bounds with constants $8$, $3$, $5$, $19$ and $25$ used in
Theorem~\ref{M-thm:switch_scaled_error}. These bounds are conclusions
of the proof, not additional assumptions on the calculation. For
example, the change in $\kappa$ is bounded algebraically by
\[
 \kappa(x)-\kappa(y)
 =(x-y)\frac{1+2x+2y+3xy}{(1+x)^2(1+y)^2},
 \qquad x,y\ge0.
\]
The fraction lies in $[0,1]$, which proves
$|\kappa(x)-\kappa(y)|\le|x-y|$ and supplies the estimate used in
the propagation of errors.

Finally, $2^{-48}=32\epsilon$ is exactly representable. The
comparisons on finite binary64 representations are proved to agree
with the strict order of their real values. Applying the error bound
gives the implications and the $57\epsilon$ separation conditions,
as in Corollary~\ref{M-cor:switch_guard}. The identity
$G=(R-L)/s$, with $s>0$, returns the assertion to the original
unscaled inequality.
\end{proof}

comparisons on finite binary64 representations are proved to agree
with the strict order of their real values. Applying the error bound
gives the implications and the $57\epsilon$ separation conditions,
as in Corollary~\ref{M-cor:switch_guard}. The identity
$G=(R-L)/s$, with $s>0$, returns the assertion to the original
unscaled inequality.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Proposition}[Error bound when the relative rounding model applies]
\label{prop:switch_raw_error}
Suppose no operation in \eqref{eq:switch_raw_evaluation} overflows,
and every nonzero exact intermediate result lies in the normal range.
With $H=\max(D,|f_3|)$,
\begin{equation}
 \bigl|(\widehat R-\widehat L)-(R-L)\bigr|
 \le 16\epsilon H.
 \label{eq:switch_raw_error}
\end{equation}
The subtraction $\widehat R-\widehat L$ in this bound is an exact
subtraction of the two computed numbers. In particular, the comparison
$\widehat L<\widehat R$ agrees with $L<R$ whenever
$|R-L|>16\epsilon H$.
\end{Proposition}

\begin{proof}
Under the stated assumptions, division of the rounded sum by two is
exact, and
\[
 |\widehat y-y_m|\le\epsilon|y_m|,\qquad
 |\widehat v-v|\le\gamma_3v\le\gamma_3/2.
\]
The quotient estimate accounts for the rounded endpoint sum, endpoint
difference and division. It follows by bounding the relative factor
$(1+\delta_1)(1+\delta_3)/(1+\delta_2)$, where
$|\delta_i|\le\epsilon$. If $y_m=0$, the corresponding quantities are
zero and the estimate remains valid.

The subtraction defining $\widehat r$ and the subsequent square give
\[
 \bigl|\widehat k-(1-\widehat v)^2\bigr|\le\gamma_3.
\]
Indeed, their relative factor contains the rounding error of the
subtraction twice and that of the multiplication once. Since
$0\le v\le1/2$ and $0\le\widehat v<1$, both $1-v$ and
$1-\widehat v$ belong to $[0,1]$. Therefore
\[
 |\widehat k-k|
 \le\gamma_3+2|\widehat v-v|
 \le2\gamma_3.
\]
Also $0\le\widehat k\le1$. For the left-hand side,
\[
 |\widehat L-L|
 \le\epsilon|f_3-\widehat y|+|\widehat y-y_m|
 \le\left(2\epsilon+\frac{\epsilon^2}{2}\right)H.
\]
For the right-hand side, the two rounded products and their rounded
sum differ from $\widehat k(|\widehat y|+|f_3|)$ by at most
$\gamma_2\widehat k(|\widehat y|+|f_3|)$. Hence
\[
 |\widehat R-R|
 \le\left[
   \frac{3+\epsilon}{2}\gamma_2
   +3\gamma_3+\frac{\epsilon}{2}
 \right]H.
\]
Adding the last two estimates gives
\[
 \bigl|(\widehat R-\widehat L)-(R-L)\bigr|
 \le\left[
   \frac{3+\epsilon}{2}\gamma_2+3\gamma_3
   +\frac{5\epsilon+\epsilon^2}{2}
 \right]H
 <16\epsilon H.
\]
This proves the bound and the assertion about the strict comparison.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
These definitions use exact real arithmetic. Since the endpoint
values have opposite signs,
\[
 v=\frac{1-\rho}{2(1+\rho)},\qquad
 k=\kappa(\rho):=
 \left(\frac{1+3\rho}{2(1+\rho)}\right)^2.
\]
The exact normalized difference is
\begin{equation}
 G=k(|h|+|p_3|)-|p_3-h|=\frac{R-L}{s}.
 \label{eq:switch_scaled_gap}
\end{equation}
Thus $G>0$ is precisely the original switching condition.

Compute the factor in the following order:
\begin{align}
 \widehat\rho
 &=\operatorname{fl}\left(
   \frac{\min(|f_1|,|f_2|)}{\max(|f_1|,|f_2|)}
   \right),\notag\\
 \widehat a&=\operatorname{fl}(1-\widehat\rho),&
 \widehat b&=\operatorname{fl}(1+\widehat\rho),\notag\\
 \widetilde v&=\operatorname{fl}\left(
    \frac{\widehat a/2}{\widehat b}\right),&
 \widetilde r&=\operatorname{fl}(1-\widetilde v),&
 \widetilde k&=\operatorname{fl}(\widetilde r^2).
 \label{eq:switch_scaled_factor}
\end{align}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Theorem}[Verified correspondence and switching decision]
\label{thm:formal_switching}
Let $w_1,w_2,w_3\in\mathcal B$, put $f_i=\nu(w_i)$, and suppose
$f_1f_2<0$. Define $\rho,s,p_i,h,G,L,R$ as in
\eqref{M-eq:switch_exact_sides}--\eqref{M-eq:switch_scaled_gap}.
Every intermediate arithmetic result in the evaluation of
$\mathcal E_{64}$ is finite, and every divisor is positive. Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
 \widehat G:=\nu\bigl(\mathcal E_{64}(w_1,w_2,w_3)\bigr)
   =\mathcal E_{\rm rn}(f_1,f_2,f_3),\qquad
 |\widehat G-G|\le25\epsilon.
 \label{eq:formal_complete_error}
\end{equation}
The executable comparisons with the binary64 representations of
$2^{-48}$ and $-2^{-48}$ consequently satisfy
\[
 \widehat G>2^{-48}\ \Longrightarrow\ L<R,
 \qquad
 \widehat G<-2^{-48}\ \Longrightarrow\ R<L.
\]
They select the respective branches whenever $G>57\epsilon$ or
$G<-57\epsilon$.
\end{Theorem}

\begin{proof}
The hypothesis implies that the endpoint magnitudes and their maximum
are positive. It follows that $s>0$, $0<\rho\le1$ and $|p_i|\le1$.
The normalized endpoint values have opposite signs. Their rounded
values retain the weak sign inequalities even if one of them becomes
zero, and hence $|\widehat p_1+\widehat p_2|\le1$.

Monotonicity of $\operatorname{rn}$ gives the intervals for the
computed factor stated in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{M-thm:switch_scaled_error}, as well as
$|\widehat h|\le1/2$. The exact results to which rounding is applied
all belong to $[-2,2]$. The endpoint maximum and $s$ are positive,
$\widehat b\ge1$, and the remaining divisor is $2$.
These facts are established before using
\eqref{eq:formal_operation_correspondence}.

Apply that relation successively to the arithmetic subexpressions.
For the initial input expressions, equality of real values is the
definition of $f_i$. If equality has already been established for the
operands of an operation, its range bound and, where needed, its
positive divisor allow \eqref{eq:formal_operation_correspondence} to
be applied. The new representation is finite and its value agrees
with the corresponding rounded real expression. Induction over the
expression therefore proves the equality in
\eqref{eq:formal_complete_error} and finiteness of all intermediate
results.

Lemma~\ref{lem:formal_rounding_error} now supplies each local absolute
error bound, and Lemma~\ref{lem:formal_factor_halving} supplies the
exact first halving. The formal real-arithmetic argument then derives
the bounds with constants $8$, $3$, $5$, $19$ and $25$ used in
Theorem~\ref{M-thm:switch_scaled_error}. These bounds are conclusions
of the proof, not additional assumptions on the calculation. For
example, the change in $\kappa$ is bounded algebraically by
\[
 \kappa(x)-\kappa(y)
 =(x-y)\frac{1+2x+2y+3xy}{(1+x)^2(1+y)^2},
 \qquad x,y\ge0.
\]
The fraction lies in $[0,1]$, which proves
$|\kappa(x)-\kappa(y)|\le|x-y|$ and supplies the estimate used in
the propagation of errors.

Finally, $2^{-48}=32\epsilon$ is exactly representable. The
comparisons on finite binary64 representations are proved to agree
with the strict order of their real values. Applying the error bound
gives the implications and the $57\epsilon$ separation conditions,
as in Corollary~\ref{M-cor:switch_guard}. The identity
$G=(R-L)/s$, with $s>0$, returns the assertion to the original
unscaled inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{Theorem}[Verified correspondence and switching decision]
\label{thm:formal_switching}
Let $w_1,w_2,w_3\in\mathcal B$, put $f_i=\nu(w_i)$, and suppose
$f_1f_2<0$. Define $\rho,s,p_i,h,G,L,R$ as in
\eqref{M-eq:switch_exact_sides}--\eqref{M-eq:switch_scaled_gap}.
Every intermediate arithmetic result in the evaluation of
$\mathcal E_{64}$ is finite, and every divisor is positive. Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
 \widehat G:=\nu\bigl(\mathcal E_{64}(w_1,w_2,w_3)\bigr)
   =\mathcal E_{\rm rn}(f_1,f_2,f_3),\qquad
 |\widehat G-G|\le25\epsilon.
 \label{eq:formal_complete_error}
\end{equation}
The executable comparisons with the binary64 representations of
$2^{-48}$ and $-2^{-48}$ consequently satisfy
\[
 \widehat G>2^{-48}\ \Longrightarrow\ L<R,
 \qquad
 \widehat G<-2^{-48}\ \Longrightarrow\ R<L.
\]
They select the respective branches whenever $G>57\epsilon$ or
$G<-57\epsilon$.
\end{Theorem}

\begin{proof}
The hypothesis implies that the endpoint magnitudes and their maximum
are positive. It follows that $s>0$, $0<\rho\le1$ and $|p_i|\le1$.
The normalized endpoint values have opposite signs. Their rounded
values retain the weak sign inequalities even if one of them becomes
zero, and hence $|\widehat p_1+\widehat p_2|\le1$.

Monotonicity of $\operatorname{rn}$ gives the intervals for the
computed factor stated in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{M-thm:switch_scaled_error}, as well as
$|\widehat h|\le1/2$. The exact results to which rounding is applied
all belong to $[-2,2]$. The endpoint maximum and $s$ are positive,
$\widehat b\ge1$, and the remaining divisor is $2$.
These facts are established before using
\eqref{eq:formal_operation_correspondence}.

Apply that relation successively to the arithmetic subexpressions.
For the initial input expressions, equality of real values is the
definition of $f_i$. If equality has already been established for the
operands of an operation, its range bound and, where needed, its
positive divisor allow \eqref{eq:formal_operation_correspondence} to
be applied. The new representation is finite and its value agrees
with the corresponding rounded real expression. Induction over the
expression therefore proves the equality in
\eqref{eq:formal_complete_error} and finiteness of all intermediate
results.

Lemma~\ref{lem:formal_rounding_error} now supplies each local absolute
error bound, and Lemma~\ref{lem:formal_factor_halving} supplies the
exact first halving. The formal real-arithmetic argument then derives
the bounds with constants $8$, $3$, $5$, $19$ and $25$ used in
Theorem~\ref{M-thm:switch_scaled_error}. These bounds are conclusions
of the proof, not additional assumptions on the calculation. For
example, the change in $\kappa$ is bounded algebraically by
\[
 \kappa(x)-\kappa(y)
 =(x-y)\frac{1+2x+2y+3xy}{(1+x)^2(1+y)^2},
 \qquad x,y\ge0.
\]
The fraction lies in $[0,1]$, which proves
$|\kappa(x)-\kappa(y)|\le|x-y|$ and supplies the estimate used in
the propagation of errors.

Finally, $2^{-48}=32\epsilon$ is exactly representable. The
comparisons on finite binary64 representations are proved to agree
with the strict order of their real values. Applying the error bound
gives the implications and the $57\epsilon$ separation conditions,
as in Corollary~\ref{M-cor:switch_guard}. The identity
$G=(R-L)/s$, with $s>0$, returns the assertion to the original
unscaled inequality.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Lemma}[A cubic bound for the switching expression]
\label{lem:switch_cubic}
Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be nonzero real endpoint values of opposite signs, and put
\begin{equation}
 D=|f_2-f_1|=|f_1|+|f_2|,\qquad
 y_m=\frac{f_1+f_2}{2},\qquad
 v=\frac{|y_m|}{D},\qquad k=(1-v)^2.
 \label{eq:cubic_definitions}
\end{equation}
For any real midpoint residual $y_3$, let $H=\max(D,|y_3|)$.
Then $0\le v\le1/2$ and, in exact arithmetic,
\begin{equation}
 k|y_m|+k|y_3|\le H(1-v)^2(1+v)\le H.
 \label{eq:cubic_switch_bound}
\end{equation}
\end{Lemma}
\begin{proof}
The triangle inequality gives
\[
 |y_m|=\tfrac12|f_1+f_2|
 \le\tfrac12(|f_1|+|f_2|)=D/2.
\]
Since $D>0$, division by $D$ gives $0\le v\le1/2$. Moreover,
\[
 k|y_m|+k|y_3|
 =(1-v)^2(vD+|y_3|)
 \le H(1-v)^2(1+v).
\]
To bound the remaining dimensionless factor, define
\[
 Q(v)=(1-v)^2(1+v)=1-v-v^2+v^3.
\]
Its derivative satisfies
\[
 Q'(v)=3v^2-2v-1=(v-1)(3v+1)<0
 \qquad (0\le v\le1/2).
\]
Thus $Q$ is decreasing, and its endpoint values yield
$3/8=Q(1/2)\le Q(v)\le Q(0)=1$.
Substitution proves \eqref{eq:cubic_switch_bound}.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Lemma}[Interiority of the AB approximation]
\label{lem:interiority}
Let $a<b$ and $uv<0$.  Then
\[
    x=\frac{av-bu}{v-u}
\]
belongs to $(a,b)$.
\end{Lemma}

\begin{proof}
Assume without loss of generality that $u<0<v$.  Then
\[
    x
    =
    \frac{av+b|u|}{v+|u|}
    =
    \lambda a+(1-\lambda)b,
    \qquad
    \lambda=\frac{v}{v+|u|}\in(0,1).
\]
Thus $x$ is a strict convex combination of $a$ and $b$ and belongs to
$(a,b)$. The case $v<0<u$ follows in the same way.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Lemma}[Preservation of the signs of the modified ordinates]
\label{lem:working_signs}
Suppose \eqref{eq:working_signs} holds.  If the retained modified ordinate is
multiplied by a finite factor $\theta>0$ and the newly inserted endpoint
receives the actual function value at the new point, then
\eqref{eq:working_signs} holds at the next nonterminating AB step.
\end{Lemma}

\begin{proof}
Multiplication by a positive factor preserves the sign of the retained
ordinate. At the new endpoint, the modified ordinate equals the actual value of the function. Since the new interval has endpoint values of opposite
signs, the modified ordinates also have opposite signs.
\end{proof}

\begin{Proposition}[Nested intervals containing a zero]
\label{prop:bracket}
At every nonterminating iteration,
\begin{equation}
    f(a_n)f(b_n)<0,
    \qquad
    I_{n+1}\subseteq I_n.
    \label{eq:nested_brackets}
\end{equation}
Consequently, every $I_n$ contains at least one zero of $f$, and the widths
\begin{equation}
    W_n=b_n-a_n
    \label{eq:width}
\end{equation}
are nonincreasing.  A bisection step gives
\begin{equation}
    W_{n+1}=\frac{1}{2}W_n.
    \label{eq:bisection_halving}
\end{equation}
\end{Proposition}

\begin{proof}
The sign condition holds initially by Assumption~\ref{ass:bracket}. The midpoint belongs
to the current interval, as does the AB approximation by
Lemma~\ref{lem:interiority}. Unless this new point is an exact zero,
precisely one of the two resulting subintervals has endpoint values of
opposite signs. The method selects this subinterval, which contains a
zero by continuity and the intermediate value theorem. This proves the
nesting property and the monotonicity of the interval lengths. A
bisection step gives a subinterval of half the preceding length.
\end{proof}

\begin{Lemma}[Decrease of the smaller endpoint residual]
\label{lem:residual_progress}
Let $R^-=\min(|f(a)|,|f(b)|)>0$ before a nonterminating step within
the interval, and let
$R^+$ be the corresponding minimum after the sign-preserving update.
If the new residual satisfies $|f(x)|<\eta R^-$ with $0<\eta<1$, then
\begin{equation}
 R^+=|f(x)|<\eta R^-.
 \label{eq:residual_contraction}
\end{equation}
For $k$ consecutive such steps, the final minimum is less than
$\eta^k$ times its initial value.
\end{Lemma}
\begin{proof}
The retained endpoint has residual magnitude at least $R^-$. The newly
inserted endpoint has residual magnitude below $\eta R^-<R^-$. It therefore
becomes the endpoint with the smaller residual magnitude, which proves
\eqref{eq:residual_contraction}. Repeated substitution proves the last claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{Lemma}[Geometric upper bound for an AB phase]
\label{lem:adaptive_envelope}
Let a phase start with width $S$, use \eqref{eq:adaptive_threshold}, and permit
at most $M$ consecutive width-test exceptions while active. If it is
still active after $t$ steps, then
\begin{equation}
 W_t\le\frac{CS}{2^t},\qquad C=2^{M+1}B.
 \label{eq:fallback_threshold}
\end{equation}
\end{Lemma}
\begin{proof}
If the width condition is satisfied at step $t$, then $W_t\le T_t$,
which is stronger than \eqref{eq:fallback_threshold}. Otherwise, let
$j=t-c$ be the last index at which it was satisfied. Since the phase
continues, $c\le M$. If the condition has not yet been satisfied, take
$j=0$ and set $T_0=2BS$; then $W_0=S\le T_0$ because $B\ge1/2$.
The bracket widths are nonincreasing, so in either case
\[
 W_t\le W_j\le T_j=2^cT_t
       \le 2^M\frac{2BS}{2^t}=\frac{CS}{2^t}.
\]
Whenever the width condition is satisfied, the counter returns to zero
and the estimate $W_j\le T_j$ holds at that index. The same argument
therefore applies after any number of such resets.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
If the width condition is satisfied at step $t$, then $W_t\le T_t$,
which is stronger than \eqref{eq:fallback_threshold}. Otherwise, let
$j=t-c$ be the last index at which it was satisfied. Since the phase
continues, $c\le M$. If the condition has not yet been satisfied, take
$j=0$ and set $T_0=2BS$; then $W_0=S\le T_0$ because $B\ge1/2$.
The bracket widths are nonincreasing, so in either case
\[
 W_t\le W_j\le T_j=2^cT_t
       \le 2^M\frac{2BS}{2^t}=\frac{CS}{2^t}.
\]
Whenever the width condition is satisfied, the counter returns to zero
and the estimate $W_j\le T_j$ holds at that index. The same argument
therefore applies after any number of such resets.
\end{proof}

\begin{Theorem}[Global convergence]
\label{thm:global_simple}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:bracket}, with the actual function values and modified ordinates
kept separate and the adaptive rule of Section~\ref{sec:method}, the
exact-arithmetic iteration, continued without an iteration limit, either
terminates at an exact zero or satisfies
\[
    W_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
In the latter case, the nested brackets shrink to a single point $x^\ast$, and that point satisfies
$f(x^\ast)=0$.
\end{Theorem}

\begin{proof}
We distinguish two cases.

\emph{Case 1: infinitely many bisection steps.}
Each bisection halves the current interval length, and no intervening AB
step increases it. After $j$ bisections the length is therefore at most
$W_0/2^j$, which tends to zero.

\emph{Case 2: finitely many bisection steps.}
After the last bisection, all subsequent steps belong to a single AB
phase. Indeed, ending that phase would require another bisection, contrary
to the choice of the last one.

Let $W_c$ be the width at the start of that phase and let $W(t)$ be the width
after $t$ AB steps.  Because the phase is still active, Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_envelope} gives
\[
    W(t)\leq \frac{C W_c}{2^t}.
\]
The right-hand side tends to zero, and hence so does $W(t)$.

Thus $W_n\to0$ in either case.  By
Proposition~\ref{prop:bracket}, the closed intervals $I_n$ are nonempty,
nested, and contain a zero.  A standard nested-interval argument now shows that
their intersection consists of one point:
\[
    \bigcap_{n=0}^{\infty} I_n=\{x^\ast\}.
\]
To verify that this point is a zero, choose any zero $z_n\in I_n$.  Both
$z_n$ and $x^\ast$ lie in the same interval, so
\[
    |z_n-x^\ast|\leq W_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus $z_n\to x^\ast$.  Since $f(z_n)=0$ and $f$ is continuous,
$f(x^\ast)=0$.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Lemma}[Guaranteed shrinkage of a completed AB phase]
\label{lem:completed_phase}
Let a completed phase block start with width $S$.  At its end the width is at
most $S/2^h$, where
\begin{equation}
    h=
    \begin{cases}
       1, & t\leq d+1,\\
       t-d, & t\geq d+2.
    \end{cases}
    \label{eq:phase_credit}
\end{equation}
In both cases,
\begin{equation}
    \ell\leq qh.
    \label{eq:length_credit}
\end{equation}
\end{Lemma}

\begin{proof}
We consider the two ranges of $t$ separately.

If $t\leq d+1$, the AB steps do not increase the interval length, and the
following bisection halves it. Thus $h=1$, and
\[
    \ell=t+1\leq d+2=q=qh.
\]

Now suppose that $t\geq d+2$.  The phase was still active after step $t-1$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_envelope} therefore gives
\[
    W(t-1)
    \leq
    \frac{CS}{2^{t-1}}
    \leq
    \frac{S}{2^{t-d-1}},
\]
where the last inequality uses $C\leq2^d$.  The $t$th AB step cannot increase
the width, and the following bisection divides it by two.  Hence
\[
    W_{\mathrm{end}}
    \leq
    \frac{S}{2^{t-d}}.
\]
The block therefore guarantees $h=t-d$ halvings.  Since $h\geq2$ and
$t=d+h$,
\[
    \ell=t+1=d+h+1\leq(d+2)h=qh.
\]
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Lemma}[An incomplete final AB phase]
\label{lem:tail}
Suppose the first $n$ iterations end either within an AB phase or
immediately after its last AB step, before the following bisection. Let $S$ be the interval length at the
start of this final AB phase. If the unfinished part has length
$\ell_{\mathrm{tail}}$, then
there is an integer $h_{\mathrm{tail}}\geq0$ such that its final width is at
most $S/2^{h_{\mathrm{tail}}}$ and
\begin{equation}
    \ell_{\mathrm{tail}}
    \leq
    qh_{\mathrm{tail}}+(q-1).
    \label{eq:tail_bound}
\end{equation}
\end{Lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $t$ be the number of AB steps in the unfinished part.

If the phase is still active and $t\leq d$, take
$h_{\mathrm{tail}}=0$.  Then
$t\leq d=q-2<q-1$.  If the phase is still active and $t\geq d+1$, Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_envelope} gives
\[
    W(t)\leq\frac{CS}{2^t}\leq\frac{S}{2^{t-d}}.
\]
Thus we may take $h_{\mathrm{tail}}=t-d$, and
$t=d+h_{\mathrm{tail}}\leq qh_{\mathrm{tail}}$.

It remains to consider a final AB step that has just triggered fallback.  If
$t\leq d+1$, again take $h_{\mathrm{tail}}=0$; then
$t\leq d+1=q-1$.  If $t\geq d+2$, the phase was active after step $t-1$, so
\[
    W(t)\leq W(t-1)
    \leq \frac{CS}{2^{t-1}}
    \leq \frac{S}{2^{t-d-1}}.
\]
Now take $h_{\mathrm{tail}}=t-d-1$.  Since
$t=h_{\mathrm{tail}}+d+1$,
\[
    t\leq qh_{\mathrm{tail}}+(q-1).
\]
These cases cover every possible unfinished final part.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Theorem}[A global bound on the interval length]
\label{thm:quantitative}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:global_simple}, after any $n$
completed bracket updates, unless an exact zero was found earlier,
\begin{equation}
    \boxed{
    W_n
    \leq
    W_0\,2^{-\lfloor n/q\rfloor},
    \qquad
    q=\lceil\log_2 C\rceil+2.
    }
    \label{eq:global_width_bound}
\end{equation}
\end{Theorem}

\begin{proof}
Partition the first $n$ iterations into:

\begin{itemize}
    \item bisection steps not already included in a completed phase block;
    \item completed phase blocks from Lemma~\ref{lem:completed_phase};
    \item at most one unfinished final part from Lemma~\ref{lem:tail}.
\end{itemize}

Let $H$ be the sum of the numbers of halvings given by these parts.
A single bisection has length $1$ and gives one halving. Each completed
phase block of length $\ell$ satisfies $\ell\leq qh$, while the
incomplete final part satisfies the bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:tail}.
Adding these inequalities gives
\begin{equation}
    n\leq qH+(q-1).
    \label{eq:amortized_sum}
\end{equation}

Because $H$ is an integer, this implies
\[
    H\geq\left\lfloor\frac{n}{q}\right\rfloor.
\]
Indeed, if $H\leq\lfloor n/q\rfloor-1$, then
\[
    n
    \leq
    q\left(\left\lfloor\frac{n}{q}\right\rfloor-1\right)+(q-1)
    <
    q\left\lfloor\frac{n}{q}\right\rfloor
    \leq n,
\]
which is impossible.  The accumulated halvings give
$W_n\leq W_0/2^H$, and the stated bound follows.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Corollary}[Finite termination for an absolute width tolerance]
\label{cor:finite_termination}
Let $\tau>0$, and suppose the method stops as soon as $W_n\leq\tau$.  Define
\[
    K=
    \max\left\{
       0,\,
       \left\lceil\log_2\frac{W_0}{\tau}\right\rceil
    \right\}.
\]
Unless an exact zero is found earlier, $W_{qK}\leq\tau$. Thus the
method terminates after at most
\begin{equation}
    N_{\max}=qK
    \label{eq:finite_bound}
\end{equation}
bracket updates.  For $C=32$, one may take $q=7$.
\end{Corollary}

\begin{proof}
If an exact zero is found earlier, the conclusion is immediate.
Otherwise, by the definition of $K$, $W_0/2^K\leq\tau$. Applying
Theorem~\ref{thm:quantitative} at $n=qK$ gives
\[
    W_{qK}
    \leq
    W_0\,2^{-\lfloor qK/q\rfloor}
    =
    \frac{W_0}{2^K}
    \leq\tau.
\]
\end{proof}

\subsection{An error bound at termination}

Let
\[
    Z=\{z\in[a_0,b_0]:f(z)=0\}
\]
be the set of all zeros in the initial bracket.  If the algorithm returns a
point $x_n\in I_n$ after a width test $W_n\leq\tau$, then
\begin{equation}
    \operatorname{dist}(x_n,Z)\leq\tau.
    \label{eq:distance_zero_set}
\end{equation}
Here $\operatorname{dist}(x_n,Z)$ means the distance from $x_n$ to the nearest
zero in $Z$.  The estimate is immediate: the current bracket contains at least
one zero $z$, and both $x_n$ and $z$ lie in an interval of width at most
$\tau$.

Using the whole zero set rather than a preselected zero is standard in
variational analysis \cite{RockafellarWets1998,DontchevRockafellar2014}.  It is
also natural for periodic functions or for a bracket containing several zeros.

A small residual $|f(x_n)|$ alone is not a scale-independent error bound.
If, however, the bracket contains a unique zero $x^\ast$, $f$ is
differentiable, and
\[
    |f'(x)|\geq m>0
\]
throughout the bracket, the mean value theorem gives

Manuscript passage
\begin{Proposition}[Error bound when the relative rounding model applies]
\label{prop:switch_raw_error}
Suppose no operation in \eqref{eq:switch_raw_evaluation} overflows,
and every nonzero exact intermediate result lies in the normal range.
With $H=\max(D,|f_3|)$,
\begin{equation}
 \bigl|(\widehat R-\widehat L)-(R-L)\bigr|
 \le 16\epsilon H.
 \label{eq:switch_raw_error}
\end{equation}
The subtraction $\widehat R-\widehat L$ in this bound is an exact
subtraction of the two computed numbers. In particular, the comparison
$\widehat L<\widehat R$ agrees with $L<R$ whenever
$|R-L|>16\epsilon H$.
\end{Proposition}

\begin{proof}
Under the stated assumptions, division of the rounded sum by two is
exact, and
\[
 |\widehat y-y_m|\le\epsilon|y_m|,\qquad
 |\widehat v-v|\le\gamma_3v\le\gamma_3/2.
\]
The quotient estimate accounts for the rounded endpoint sum, endpoint
difference and division. It follows by bounding the relative factor
$(1+\delta_1)(1+\delta_3)/(1+\delta_2)$, where
$|\delta_i|\le\epsilon$. If $y_m=0$, the corresponding quantities are
zero and the estimate remains valid.

The subtraction defining $\widehat r$ and the subsequent square give
\[
 \bigl|\widehat k-(1-\widehat v)^2\bigr|\le\gamma_3.
\]
Indeed, their relative factor contains the rounding error of the
subtraction twice and that of the multiplication once. Since
$0\le v\le1/2$ and $0\le\widehat v<1$, both $1-v$ and
$1-\widehat v$ belong to $[0,1]$. Therefore
\[
 |\widehat k-k|
 \le\gamma_3+2|\widehat v-v|
 \le2\gamma_3.
\]
Also $0\le\widehat k\le1$. For the left-hand side,
\[
 |\widehat L-L|
 \le\epsilon|f_3-\widehat y|+|\widehat y-y_m|
 \le\left(2\epsilon+\frac{\epsilon^2}{2}\right)H.
\]
For the right-hand side, the two rounded products and their rounded
sum differ from $\widehat k(|\widehat y|+|f_3|)$ by at most
$\gamma_2\widehat k(|\widehat y|+|f_3|)$. Hence
\[
 |\widehat R-R|
 \le\left[
   \frac{3+\epsilon}{2}\gamma_2
   +3\gamma_3+\frac{\epsilon}{2}
 \right]H.
\]
Adding the last two estimates gives
\[
 \bigl|(\widehat R-\widehat L)-(R-L)\bigr|
 \le\left[
   \frac{3+\epsilon}{2}\gamma_2+3\gamma_3
   +\frac{5\epsilon+\epsilon^2}{2}
 \right]H
 <16\epsilon H.
\]
This proves the bound and the assertion about the strict comparison.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Proposition}[A one-sided quadratic AB phase]
\label{prop:one_sided}
For the continuously differentiable function
\begin{equation}
 f(x)=\begin{cases}x,&x\le0,\\x+x^2,&x>0,\end{cases}
 \label{eq:one_sided_function}
\end{equation}
an AB phase starting from $[-1,1]$ with the actual endpoint values as its
initial ordinates has a fixed
right endpoint. If interpolation is continued without a width fallback,
the left-endpoint error converges quadratically to zero, whereas the bracket
width tends to one.
\end{Proposition}
\begin{proof}
Write the left endpoint as $-e$ and the right modified ordinate as $v>1$.
The actual left ordinate is $-e$. The next secant approximation is $-e'$, where
\[
 e'=\frac{e(v-1)}{v+e}>0.
\]
Starting with $e=1,v=2$, the first two errors are $1/3$ and $1/7$.
\rev{The second consecutive update of the left endpoint activates the AB correction.} Whenever it is applied,
\[
 v'=v\left(1-\frac{e'}e\right)
    =\frac{v(1+e)}{v+e}=1+e'.
\]
Thus the next trial point remains to the left and, from the error $1/7$ onward,
\begin{equation}
 e_{k+1}=\frac{e_k^2}{1+2e_k}.
 \label{eq:one_sided_quadratic}
\end{equation}
This positive sequence decreases to zero and
$e_{k+1}/e_k^2\to1$. Its first subsequent values are $1/63$, $1/4095$ and
$1/16777215$. The right endpoint stays at one, so $W_k=1+e_k\to1$.
\end{proof}

Manuscript passage
\begin{Proposition}[Residual contraction without width convergence]
\label{prop:uncapped_counterexample}
Consider the usual AB correction, the switching test
\eqref{eq:switch_test}, and the rule with $B=2$, $\eta=1/2$, but with
no bound on the number of residual exceptions. For
\begin{equation}
 f(x)=\begin{cases}-x^2,&x<0,\\7x^2,&x\ge0,\end{cases}
 \qquad [a_0,b_0]=[-3,1],
 \label{eq:cap_counterexample}
\end{equation}
the exact-arithmetic process enters an AB phase after its first bisection
and never leaves it. The left endpoints converge to the unique
zero, while the right endpoint remains $1$ and the width tends to $1$.
From the third AB step onward, the ratio of the new residual magnitude to
the smaller preceding endpoint residual magnitude is at most $0.49<1/2$.
The function belongs to $C^1(\mathbb R)$.
\end{Proposition}

\begin{proof}
The only zero is $0$. On the two open half-lines the derivatives are $-2x$
and $14x$, respectively. At zero,
$f'(0)=\lim_{h\to0}f(h)/h=0$, and both one-sided derivatives tend to zero.
This proves the stated regularity.

Initially $f(-3)=-9$ and $f(1)=7$. The first midpoint is $-1$, with
$f(-1)=-1$, and the chord midpoint value is also $(-9+7)/2=-1$.
Consequently, the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:switch_test} is zero and
its right-hand side is positive. The method enters AB on $[-1,1]$.

Let $j$ count AB steps after this entry. Write the left endpoint as $-e_j$
and the retained right modified ordinate as $v_j$, with $e_0=1$ and $v_0=7$.
The actual function value at the left endpoint is $-e_j^2$. If the next trial point remains to the
left of the zero, the secant formula gives
\begin{equation}
 e_j=\frac{e_{j-1}v_{j-1}-e_{j-1}^2}
              {v_{j-1}+e_{j-1}^2}.
 \label{eq:cap_secant_error}
\end{equation}
\revb{The switching bisection replaced the left endpoint, $e_0=1$, and the first
AB step replaces it again. The retained right ordinate is therefore rescaled
already at the first AB step. Hence
\[
 e_1=\frac{7-1}{7+1}=\frac34,\qquad v_1=7\Bigl(1-\frac{e_1^2}{e_0^2}\Bigr)=\frac{49}{16},
 \qquad e_2=\frac{v_1e_1-e_1^2}{v_1+e_1^2}=\frac{111}{232}.
\]}
Both approximations lie strictly to the left of zero and are closer to
it than the preceding left endpoint.

For two successive updates of that endpoint, the AB multiplier is
$1-e_j^2/e_{j-1}^2$, which is positive whenever $0<e_j<e_{j-1}$.
Rearranging \eqref{eq:cap_secant_error} gives
\[
 (e_{j-1}-e_j)v_{j-1}=e_{j-1}^2(1+e_j).
\]
Thus, for $j\ge\revb{1}$ while these inequalities hold,
\begin{align}
 v_j
 &=v_{j-1}\left(1-\frac{e_j^2}{e_{j-1}^2}\right)\notag\\
 &=\frac{e_{j-1}^2(1+e_j)}{e_{j-1}-e_j}
   \frac{(e_{j-1}-e_j)(e_{j-1}+e_j)}{e_{j-1}^2}\notag\\
 &=(1+e_j)(e_{j-1}+e_j).
 \label{eq:cap_working_ordinate}
\end{align}
Applying this identity at $j=2$ and then taking the next secant yields
\[
 e_3=\revb{\frac{2664111}{8512544}},\qquad
 \rho_3:=\frac{e_3}{e_2}=\revb{\frac{24001}{36692}}.
\]
In particular, $0<e_3<2/5$ and $1/2<\rho_3<7/10$.

To prove that all subsequent approximations have the same properties, put $\rho_j=e_j/e_{j-1}$.
Using \eqref{eq:cap_working_ordinate} in the next secant, we obtain
\begin{align*}
 \frac{e_{j+1}}{e_j}
 &=\frac{v_j-e_j}{v_j+e_j^2}\\
 &=\frac{(1+e_j)e_{j-1}+e_j^2}
         {(1+e_j)e_{j-1}+e_j+2e_j^2}\\
 &=\frac{1+e_j(1+\rho_j)}
         {1+\rho_j+e_j(1+2\rho_j)}.
\end{align*}
The last equality divides numerator and denominator by $e_{j-1}>0$.
Define
\[
 \Phi(e,\rho)=\frac{1+e(1+\rho)}{1+\rho+e(1+2\rho)}.
\]
For $e\ge0$ and $\rho>0$ its denominator is positive, and direct
differentiation gives
\[
 \frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial\rho}
 =-\frac{(1+e)^2}{[1+\rho+e(1+2\rho)]^2}<0,\qquad
 \frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial e}
 =\frac{\rho^2}{[1+\rho+e(1+2\rho)]^2}>0.
\]
On $0\le e\le2/5$, $1/2\le\rho\le7/10$, monotonicity therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 \frac{10}{17}=\Phi(0,7/10)
 \le\Phi(e,\rho)\le\Phi(2/5,1/2)=\frac{16}{23}<\frac7{10}.
 \label{eq:cap_invariant_region}
\end{equation}
Both bounds belong to $[1/2,7/10]$. Since the required inequalities hold
for $j=3$, induction gives
\[
 0<e_{j+1}\le\tfrac7{10}e_j,\qquad
 \rho_{j+1}\in[1/2,7/10].
\]
These inequalities simultaneously prove that the next trial point remains
strictly left of zero, that the AB multiplier stays positive, and that
the hypotheses are preserved. Thus $e_j\to0$ and the right endpoint
is never replaced.

The actual value of the function at the right endpoint is $7$ and the left residual magnitude is
$e_j^2\le1$. Before AB step $j$ the minimum residual magnitude is therefore
$e_{j-1}^2$. For every $j\ge3$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{|f(-e_j)|}{\min\{|f(-e_{j-1})|,|f(1)|\}}
 =\rho_j^2\le(7/10)^2=0.49<\tfrac12.
 \label{eq:cap_residual_ratio}
\end{equation}

At the beginning of the phase the width is $S=2$, so the threshold at AB step $j$ is
$T_j=4/2^{j-1}$. The first two interval lengths satisfy the respective bounds
$4$ and $2$. For $j\ge3$, however, $T_j\le1$ while
$W_j^{\rm AB}=1+e_j>1$. The width condition is therefore violated at every subsequent step,
whereas \eqref{eq:cap_residual_ratio} permits a residual exception at each
of these steps. Without a bound on their number, the AB phase continues
indefinitely and the interval length tends to $1$.
\end{proof}

Applying this identity at $j=2$ and then taking the next secant yields
\[

 \rho_3:=\frac{e_3}{e_2}=\revb{\frac{24001}{36692}}.
\]
In particular, $0<e_3<2/5$ and $1/2<\rho_3<7/10$.

To prove that all subsequent approximations have the same properties, put $\rho_j=e_j/e_{j-1}$.

 &=\frac{(1+e_j)e_{j-1}+e_j^2}
         {(1+e_j)e_{j-1}+e_j+2e_j^2}\\
 &=\frac{1+e_j(1+\rho_j)}
         {1+\rho_j+e_j(1+2\rho_j)}.
\end{align*}
The last equality divides numerator and denominator by $e_{j-1}>0$.

\[
 \Phi(e,\rho)=\frac{1+e(1+\rho)}{1+\rho+e(1+2\rho)}.

For $e\ge0$ and $\rho>0$ its denominator is positive, and direct
differentiation gives
\[

 =-\frac{(1+e)^2}{[1+\rho+e(1+2\rho)]^2}<0,\qquad

 \label{eq:cap_invariant_region}

Both bounds belong to $[1/2,7/10]$. Since the required inequalities hold

\[

\]

strictly left of zero, that the AB multiplier stays positive, and that

is never replaced.

$e_j^2\le1$. Before AB step $j$ the minimum residual magnitude is therefore
$e_{j-1}^2$. For every $j\ge3$,

\end{equation}

$T_j=4/2^{j-1}$. The first two interval lengths satisfy the respective bounds

\begin{Proposition}[Residual contraction without width convergence]
\label{prop:uncapped_counterexample}
Consider the usual AB correction, the switching test
\eqref{eq:switch_test}, and the rule with $B=2$, $\eta=1/2$, but with
no bound on the number of residual exceptions. For
\begin{equation}
 f(x)=\begin{cases}-x^2,&x<0,\\7x^2,&x\ge0,\end{cases}
 \qquad [a_0,b_0]=[-3,1],
 \label{eq:cap_counterexample}
\end{equation}
the exact-arithmetic process enters an AB phase after its first bisection
and never leaves it. The left endpoints converge to the unique
zero, while the right endpoint remains $1$ and the width tends to $1$.
From the third AB step onward, the ratio of the new residual magnitude to
the smaller preceding endpoint residual magnitude is at most $0.49<1/2$.
The function belongs to $C^1(\mathbb R)$.
\end{Proposition}

\begin{proof}
The only zero is $0$. On the two open half-lines the derivatives are $-2x$
and $14x$, respectively. At zero,
$f'(0)=\lim_{h\to0}f(h)/h=0$, and both one-sided derivatives tend to zero.
This proves the stated regularity.

Initially $f(-3)=-9$ and $f(1)=7$. The first midpoint is $-1$, with
$f(-1)=-1$, and the chord midpoint value is also $(-9+7)/2=-1$.
Consequently, the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:switch_test} is zero and
its right-hand side is positive. The method enters AB on $[-1,1]$.

Let $j$ count AB steps after this entry. Write the left endpoint as $-e_j$
and the retained right modified ordinate as $v_j$, with $e_0=1$ and $v_0=7$.
The actual function value at the left endpoint is $-e_j^2$. If the next trial point remains to the
left of the zero, the secant formula gives
\begin{equation}
 e_j=\frac{e_{j-1}v_{j-1}-e_{j-1}^2}
              {v_{j-1}+e_{j-1}^2}.
 \label{eq:cap_secant_error}
\end{equation}
\revb{The switching bisection replaced the left endpoint, $e_0=1$, and the first
AB step replaces it again. The retained right ordinate is therefore rescaled
already at the first AB step. Hence
\[
 e_1=\frac{7-1}{7+1}=\frac34,\qquad v_1=7\Bigl(1-\frac{e_1^2}{e_0^2}\Bigr)=\frac{49}{16},
 \qquad e_2=\frac{v_1e_1-e_1^2}{v_1+e_1^2}=\frac{111}{232}.
\]}
Both approximations lie strictly to the left of zero and are closer to
it than the preceding left endpoint.

For two successive updates of that endpoint, the AB multiplier is
$1-e_j^2/e_{j-1}^2$, which is positive whenever $0<e_j<e_{j-1}$.
Rearranging \eqref{eq:cap_secant_error} gives
\[
 (e_{j-1}-e_j)v_{j-1}=e_{j-1}^2(1+e_j).
\]
Thus, for $j\ge\revb{1}$ while these inequalities hold,
\begin{align}
 v_j
 &=v_{j-1}\left(1-\frac{e_j^2}{e_{j-1}^2}\right)\notag\\
 &=\frac{e_{j-1}^2(1+e_j)}{e_{j-1}-e_j}
   \frac{(e_{j-1}-e_j)(e_{j-1}+e_j)}{e_{j-1}^2}\notag\\
 &=(1+e_j)(e_{j-1}+e_j).
 \label{eq:cap_working_ordinate}
\end{align}
Applying this identity at $j=2$ and then taking the next secant yields
\[
 e_3=\revb{\frac{2664111}{8512544}},\qquad
 \rho_3:=\frac{e_3}{e_2}=\revb{\frac{24001}{36692}}.
\]
In particular, $0<e_3<2/5$ and $1/2<\rho_3<7/10$.

To prove that all subsequent approximations have the same properties, put $\rho_j=e_j/e_{j-1}$.
Using \eqref{eq:cap_working_ordinate} in the next secant, we obtain
\begin{align*}
 \frac{e_{j+1}}{e_j}
 &=\frac{v_j-e_j}{v_j+e_j^2}\\
 &=\frac{(1+e_j)e_{j-1}+e_j^2}
         {(1+e_j)e_{j-1}+e_j+2e_j^2}\\
 &=\frac{1+e_j(1+\rho_j)}
         {1+\rho_j+e_j(1+2\rho_j)}.
\end{align*}
The last equality divides numerator and denominator by $e_{j-1}>0$.
Define
\[
 \Phi(e,\rho)=\frac{1+e(1+\rho)}{1+\rho+e(1+2\rho)}.
\]
For $e\ge0$ and $\rho>0$ its denominator is positive, and direct
differentiation gives
\[
 \frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial\rho}
 =-\frac{(1+e)^2}{[1+\rho+e(1+2\rho)]^2}<0,\qquad
 \frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial e}
 =\frac{\rho^2}{[1+\rho+e(1+2\rho)]^2}>0.
\]
On $0\le e\le2/5$, $1/2\le\rho\le7/10$, monotonicity therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 \frac{10}{17}=\Phi(0,7/10)
 \le\Phi(e,\rho)\le\Phi(2/5,1/2)=\frac{16}{23}<\frac7{10}.
 \label{eq:cap_invariant_region}
\end{equation}
Both bounds belong to $[1/2,7/10]$. Since the required inequalities hold
for $j=3$, induction gives
\[
 0<e_{j+1}\le\tfrac7{10}e_j,\qquad
 \rho_{j+1}\in[1/2,7/10].
\]
These inequalities simultaneously prove that the next trial point remains
strictly left of zero, that the AB multiplier stays positive, and that
the hypotheses are preserved. Thus $e_j\to0$ and the right endpoint
is never replaced.

The actual value of the function at the right endpoint is $7$ and the left residual magnitude is
$e_j^2\le1$. Before AB step $j$ the minimum residual magnitude is therefore
$e_{j-1}^2$. For every $j\ge3$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{|f(-e_j)|}{\min\{|f(-e_{j-1})|,|f(1)|\}}
 =\rho_j^2\le(7/10)^2=0.49<\tfrac12.
 \label{eq:cap_residual_ratio}
\end{equation}

At the beginning of the phase the width is $S=2$, so the threshold at AB step $j$ is
$T_j=4/2^{j-1}$. The first two interval lengths satisfy the respective bounds
$4$ and $2$. For $j\ge3$, however, $T_j\le1$ while
$W_j^{\rm AB}=1+e_j>1$. The width condition is therefore violated at every subsequent step,
whereas \eqref{eq:cap_residual_ratio} permits a residual exception at each
of these steps. Without a bound on their number, the AB phase continues
indefinitely and the interval length tends to $1$.
\end{proof}

step is never rescaled, the same argument applies with $v_1=7$,
$e_2=75/121$, $e_3=146325/384296$ and $\rho_3=1951/3176$.

The same example shows that the earlier global estimate cannot be
retained after removing the bound on consecutive exceptions. If $N$ counts all bracket updates,
including the initial bisection, then $W_0=4$ and
\begin{equation}
 W_{14}=1+e_{13}>1
       =W_0\,2^{-\lfloor14/7\rfloor}.
 \label{eq:cap_global_violation}
\end{equation}
The approximations themselves still converge to the zero. What fails is
convergence of the whole bracket and, consequently, width-based termination
at a tolerance below the limiting width. For the mixed tolerance used here,
any fixed $\varepsilon_{\rm abs}<1$ and finite $\varepsilon_{\rm rel}$
leave the width test unsatisfied for all sufficiently late steps, since the
candidate tends to zero. In particular, the tolerances of the numerical
experiment in Section~\ref{subsec:native_cap} cannot terminate this
exact-arithmetic process by width. It never encounters an exact zero.
\end{revision}

\section{Implementation and Reliable Stopping}
\label{sec:implementation}

In the C\# implementation, the endpoint coordinates are stored in
\texttt{p1.X} and \texttt{p2.X}. The fields \texttt{p1.Y} and \texttt{p2.Y}
retain the actual function values $\alpha$ and $\beta$, whereas the local
variables \texttt{f1} and \texttt{f2} hold the modified ordinates $u$ and $v$.  This separation is
the main correction.  A change to $u$ or $v$ changes the next interpolation
point; it must not change which signs define the bracket.

theorem · ModAB/Binary64.lean:95–119

lem:formal_rounding_error

Separates 0 and ±2; inside the range proves magnitude≤1, exponent≤−52, ulp≤2⁻⁵², and half-ulp≤ε.

Steps: R2

Lean declaration and proof
theorem round_error {x : ℝ} (hx : |x| ≤ 2) : Within (round x) x binary64Epsilon := by
  by_cases h0 : x = 0
  · subst x; simpa [Within] using le_of_lt binary64Epsilon_pos
  by_cases hp : x = 2
  · subst x; simpa [Within] using le_of_lt binary64Epsilon_pos
  by_cases hn : x = -2
  · subst x; simpa [Within] using le_of_lt binary64Epsilon_pos
  have hlt : |x| < 2 := by
    rcases le_total 0 x with h | h
    · rw [abs_of_nonneg h] at hx ⊢; exact lt_of_le_of_ne hx hp
    · rw [abs_of_nonpos h] at hx ⊢; exact lt_of_le_of_ne hx (by intro he; apply hn; linarith)
  have hmag : magnitude binaryRadix x ≤ 1 :=
    magnitude_le_of_abs_lt_bpow binaryRadix x 1 h0 (by simpa [pow_value] using hlt)
  have hexp : cexp binaryRadix exponent x ≤ -52 := by
    dsimp [cexp, exponent, fltExp]
    exact max_le (by omega) (by norm_num)
  have hpw := (bpow_le_bpow_iff binaryRadix _ _).mpr hexp
  have hu : ulp binaryRadix exponent x ≤ (2:ℝ)^(-52:ℤ) := by
    rw [ulp.of_ne_zero _ _ _ h0]
    simpa [pow_value] using hpw
  have he := error_bound_ulp (β := binaryRadix) (fexp := exponent) nearestEven x
  change |round x-x| ≤ _ at he
  apply le_trans he
  have h := div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hu (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 2)
  convert h using 1 <;> norm_num [binary64Epsilon]

theorem residual_progress_iterated {R : ℕ→ℝ} {η : ℝ} (hη : 0<η)
    (h : ∀ n, R (n+1)<η*R n) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0<k) : R k<η^k*R 0 := by
  cases k with
  | zero => omega
  | succ k =>

      | succ k ih =>

               _<η*(η^(k+1)*R 0):=hmul

    (hx : ∀n,x∈Icc (a n) (b n)) (hz : ∀n,z n∈Icc (a n) (b n))

  have hsmall:=hN n hn

theorem · ModAB/Bracketing.lean:120–148

thm:global_simple

Uses the standard compact nested-interval theorem, proves the intersection is a singleton by shrinking width, chooses a zero in each interval, and uses continuity on the initial interval.

Steps: G3, G4

Lean declaration and proof
theorem nested_intervals_root {f : ℝ→ℝ} {a b : ℕ→ℝ}
    (hnested : ∀n,Icc (a (n+1)) (b (n+1))⊆Icc (a n) (b n))
    (hzero : ∀n,∃z∈Icc (a n) (b n),f z=0)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc (a 0) (b 0)))
    (hw : Tendsto (fun n=>b n-a n) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    ∃x, (⋂n,Icc (a n) (b n))={x} ∧ f x=0 := by
  have hne : ∀n,(Icc (a n) (b n)).Nonempty := fun n=>by
    obtain ⟨z,hz,_⟩:=hzero n; exact ⟨z,hz⟩
  obtain ⟨x,hx⟩:=IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_sequence_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed
    (fun n=>Icc (a n) (b n)) hnested hne isCompact_Icc (fun _=>isClosed_Icc)
  have hxall : ∀n,x∈Icc (a n) (b n) := mem_iInter.mp hx
  have hinter : (⋂n,Icc (a n) (b n))={x} := by
    apply Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.mpr
    refine ⟨hx,?_⟩
    intro y hy
    have hyall:=mem_iInter.mp hy
    have hlim:=chosen_points_tendsto hxall hyall hw
    exact tendsto_nhds_unique tendsto_const_nhds hlim
  choose z hz hval using hzero
  have hzlim:=chosen_points_tendsto hxall hz hw
  have hmono : Antitone (fun n=>Icc (a n) (b n)):=antitone_nat_of_succ_le hnested
  have hz0 : ∀n,z n∈Icc (a 0) (b 0):=fun n=>hmono (Nat.zero_le n) (hz n)
  have hcont : Tendsto (fun n=>f (z n)) atTop (𝓝 (f x)) :=
    (hf x (hxall 0)).tendsto.comp (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff.mpr ⟨hzlim,Filter.Eventually.of_forall hz0⟩)
  have heq : f x=0 := by
    have he : (fun n=>f (z n))=(fun _ : ℕ=>0) := funext hval
    rw [he] at hcont
    exact (tendsto_nhds_unique tendsto_const_nhds hcont).symm
  exact ⟨x,hinter,heq⟩

theorem switching_bound {f1 f2 : ℝ} (hs : f1*f2<0) (f3 : ℝ) :
    let D := |f2-f1|
    let y := (f1+f2)/2
    let v := |y|/D
    let H := max D |f3|
    (1-v)^2*|y|+(1-v)^2*|f3| ≤ H*Q v ∧ H*Q v ≤ H := by
  dsimp only
  let D := |f2-f1|
  let y := (f1+f2)/2
  let v := |y|/D
  let H := max D |f3|
  change (1-v)^2*|y|+(1-v)^2*|f3| ≤ H*Q v ∧ H*Q v ≤ H
  have hd : 0<D := endpoint_difference_pos hs
  have hv : v ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) (1/2) := ratio_range hs
  have hDH : D≤H := le_max_left _ _
  have hzH : |f3|≤H := le_max_right _ _
  have hH : 0≤H := (le_of_lt hd).trans hDH
  have hyv : |y|=v*D := by dsimp [v]; field_simp
  have hsum : |y|+|f3|≤H*(v+1) := by
    rw [hyv]
    nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hDH hv.1]
  constructor
  · have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsum (sq_nonneg (1-v))
    dsimp [Q]
    nlinarith only [h]
  · exact (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Q_bounds hv).2 hH).trans_eq (mul_one H)

prop:one_sided, prop:uncapped_counterexample

Induction gives eₙ≤rⁿe₀; the geometric limit and a squeeze argument yield eₙ→0. No convergence assumption is built into the recurrence.

theorem geometric_bound {e : ℕ→ℝ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0≤r)
    (hs : ∀n,e (n+1)≤r*e n) : ∀n,e n≤r^n*e 0 := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero=>simp
  | succ n ih=>
    calc
      e (n+1)≤r*e n:=hs n
      _≤r*(r^n*e 0):=mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ih hr
      _=r^(n+1)*e 0:=by rw [pow_succ]; ring

lemma · ModAB/Expressions.lean:20–43

eq:formal_operation_correspondence

Exact absolute value and finite minimum/maximum; semantic min/max equalities are taken from FloatLib in the structural proof.

Steps: F3

Lean declaration and proof
lemma abs_value (x : Word) (hx : valid x) : value (Model.abs x) = |value x| := by
  have hsigned : FloatFormat.binary64.supportsSignedZero = true := by decide
  obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := Model.exists_toDyadic?_of_isFinite hx
  have hsign := Model.sign_eq_signBit_of_toDyadic?_some hd
  have hreal : value x = d.toReal := by simp [Model.toReal_eq, hd]
  have hp := FloatLib.Floats.Formats.Flocq.bpow.pos FloatLib.Numerics.binaryRadix d.exponent
  cases hs : Model.signBit x with
  | false =>
    have hn : 0 ≤ value x := by
      rw [hreal]
      simp only [FloatLib.Numerics.Dyadic.toReal, FloatLib.Numerics.Dyadic.signedSignificand,
        hsign.trans hs, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte]
      exact mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) hp.le
    simpa [Model.abs, Model.copySign, hsigned, hs] using (abs_of_nonneg hn).symm
  | true =>
    have hn : value x ≤ 0 := by
      rw [hreal]
      simp only [FloatLib.Numerics.Dyadic.toReal, FloatLib.Numerics.Dyadic.signedSignificand,
        hsign.trans hs, ↓reduceIte, Int.cast_neg]
      exact mul_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg (neg_nonpos.mpr (Nat.cast_nonneg _)) hp.le
    have habs : Model.abs x = Model.neg x := by
      simp [Model.abs, Model.copySign, Model.neg, hs]
    change Model.toReal (Model.abs x) = |Model.toReal x|
    rw [habs, Model.toReal_neg x hx, abs_of_nonpos hn]

theorem · ModAB/Expressions.lean:107–138

thm:formal_switching

Structural induction: inputs/constants, abs/min/max, then four arithmetic operations. Proves finiteness of subtrees while identifying their values.

Steps: F4

Lean declaration and proof
theorem expression_refines (e : Expr) (env : Nat → Word)
    (hi : ∀ i, valid (env i)) (hs : e.Safe (fun i => value (env i))) :
    valid (e.bits env) ∧ value (e.bits env) = e.real (fun i => value (env i)) := by
  induction e with
  | input i => exact ⟨hi i, rfl⟩
  | one => exact ⟨one_valid, one_value⟩
  | two => exact ⟨two_valid, two_value⟩
  | abs x ih =>
    obtain ⟨hx, he⟩ := ih hs
    exact ⟨by simpa only [Expr.bits, valid, Model.isFinite_abs] using hx,
      by simpa only [Expr.bits, Expr.real, he] using abs_value (x.bits env) hx⟩
  | min x y ihx ihy =>
    obtain ⟨hx, ex⟩ := ihx hs.1
    obtain ⟨hy, ey⟩ := ihy hs.2
    exact ⟨min_valid _ _ hx hy, by simpa only [Expr.bits, Expr.real, ex, ey] using
      Model.toReal_minimum_eq_min_of_isFinite (x.bits env) (y.bits env) hx hy⟩
  | max x y ihx ihy =>
    obtain ⟨hx, ex⟩ := ihx hs.1
    obtain ⟨hy, ey⟩ := ihy hs.2
    exact ⟨max_valid _ _ hx hy, by simpa only [Expr.bits, Expr.real, ex, ey] using
      Model.toReal_maximum_eq_max_of_isFinite (x.bits env) (y.bits env) hx hy⟩
  | op o x y ihx ihy =>
    obtain ⟨hx, ex⟩ := ihx hs.1
    obtain ⟨hy, ey⟩ := ihy hs.2.1
    have hb : |o.exact (value (x.bits env)) (value (y.bits env))| ≤ 2 := by
      rw [ex, ey]; exact hs.2.2.1
    have hd : o = .div → value (y.bits env) ≠ 0 := by rw [ey]; exact hs.2.2.2
    cases o with
    | add => simpa only [Expr.bits, Expr.real, Op.bits, Op.exact, ex, ey] using add_refines _ _ hx hy hb
    | sub => simpa only [Expr.bits, Expr.real, Op.bits, Op.exact, ex, ey] using sub_refines _ _ hx hy hb
    | mul => simpa only [Expr.bits, Expr.real, Op.bits, Op.exact, ex, ey] using mul_refines _ _ hx hy hb
    | div => simpa only [Expr.bits, Expr.real, Op.bits, Op.exact, ex, ey] using div_refines _ _ hx hy (hd rfl) hb

inductive Step (B : ℝ) (M : ℕ) : ℝ → Mode → ℝ → Mode → Prop
  | bisectStay (w) : Step B M w .bisection (w/2) .bisection
  | bisectStart (w) : Step B M w .bisection (w/2) (.ab (w/2) 0 0)
  | abWidth {w w' S t c} : 0≤w' → w'≤w → w'≤threshold B S (t+1) →
      Step B M w (.ab S t c) w' (.ab S (t+1) 0)
  | abException {w w' S t c} : 0≤w' → w'≤w → threshold B S (t+1)<w' → c<M →
      Step B M w (.ab S t c) w' (.ab S (t+1) (c+1))
  | abStop {w w' S t c} : 0≤w' → w'≤w → Step B M w (.ab S t c) w' .bisection

    (hs : Step B M w m w' m') (hw : w≤W0/(2:ℝ)^k) :

theorem finite_bisections {B : ℝ} {M : ℕ} (hB : (1/2:ℝ)≤B) (r : Run B M)
    (h : ¬∀N,∃n,N≤n ∧ isBisection (r.mode n)=true) :
    Tendsto r.width atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  push_neg at h
  obtain ⟨N,hN⟩:=h
  have hno : ∀n,N≤n→isBisection (r.mode n)=false := by
    intro n hn
    exact Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr (hN n hn)
  obtain ⟨S,t,c,hm,hS,ha⟩:=active_history r.nonneg_initial (history_of_run r N) (hno N (le_refl N))
  have hs:=continuing_suffix r hm ha hno
  have hlim : Tendsto (fun k=>r.width (N+k)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    apply squeeze_zero (fun k=>run_nonnegative r (N+k))
      (fun k=>?_) (dyadic_tendsto (envelopeConstant B M*S/(2:ℝ)^t))
    obtain ⟨c',hm',ha'⟩:=hs k
    have hb:=active_envelope hB hS ha'
    simpa only [pow_add,div_mul_eq_div_div] using hb
  exact (tendsto_add_atTop_iff_nat N).mp (by simpa [Nat.add_comm] using hlim)

    leftStep 1 ⟨e,1+e,true⟩=⟨quadraticMap e,1+quadraticMap e,true⟩ := by
  have hd : 1+2*e≠0:=ne_of_gt (by positivity)

  have ht : leftTrial 1 e (1+e)=quadraticMap e:=by

    dsimp [quadraticMap]
    congr 1 <;> ring
  have hc:=one_correction_identity he (show 1<1+e by linarith)
  simp only [leftStep,pow_one,ite_true]
  rw [hc.1,hc.2,ht]

theorem domain_iff_product_negative (env : ℕ→ℝ) : Domain env ↔ env 0*env 1<0 := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h0,h1,h⟩
    rcases h with ⟨ha,hb⟩|⟨hb,ha⟩
    · exact mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos (lt_of_le_of_ne ha h0) (lt_of_le_of_ne hb (Ne.symm h1))
    · exact mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg (lt_of_le_of_ne ha (Ne.symm h0)) (lt_of_le_of_ne hb h1)
  · intro h
    have h0 : env 0≠0 := by intro hz; simp [hz] at h
    have h1 : env 1≠0 := by intro hz; simp [hz] at h
    refine ⟨h0,h1,?_⟩
    rcases mul_neg_iff.mp h with h|h
    · exact Or.inr ⟨h.2.le,h.1.le⟩
    · exact Or.inl ⟨h.1.le,h.2.le⟩

lem:adaptive_envelope, rem:proof_independence

Continuing phase transitions: width success resets c; width failure is allowed only if c<M. The residual test can only restrict these exceptions.

inductive ActivePhase (B : ℝ) (M : ℕ) (S : ℝ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ → Prop
  | start : ActivePhase B M S 0 0 S
  | width {t c : ℕ} {w w' : ℝ} :
      ActivePhase B M S t c w → 0≤w' → w'≤w → w'≤threshold B S (t+1) →
      ActivePhase B M S (t+1) 0 w'
  | exception {t c : ℕ} {w w' : ℝ} :
      ActivePhase B M S t c w → 0≤w' → w'≤w → threshold B S (t+1)<w' → c<M →
      ActivePhase B M S (t+1) (c+1) w'

theorem completed_phase {B S u v : ℝ} {M t c d : ℕ}
    (hB : (1/2:ℝ)≤B) (hS : 0≤S) (hC : envelopeConstant B M≤(2:ℝ)^d)
    (ht : 1≤t) (hphase : ActivePhase B M S (t-1) c u) (huv : v≤u) :
    v/2≤S/(2:ℝ)^(phaseCredit d t) ∧ t+1≤(d+2)*phaseCredit d t := by
  by_cases hshort : t≤d+1
  · simp only [phaseCredit,if_pos hshort,pow_one]
    exact ⟨div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (huv.trans (active_nonincrease hphase)) (by norm_num),by omega⟩
  · have hlong : d≤t-1 := by omega
    have hw := envelope_to_dyadic hB hS hC hphase hlong
    have he : t-d=(t-1-d)+1 := by omega
    have hratio : (S/(2:ℝ)^(t-1-d))/2=S/(2:ℝ)^(t-d) := by rw [he,pow_succ]; ring
    simp only [phaseCredit,if_neg hshort]
    constructor
    · exact (div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (huv.trans hw) (by norm_num)).trans_eq hratio
    · have hh : 2≤t-d := by omega
      have hm := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (d+1) (show 1≤t-d by omega)
      have htde : t=d+(t-d) := by omega

theorem · ModAB/Residual.lean:21–43

eq:residual_bound

Applies the mean-value bound on the subinterval between x and a selected zero z and divides by m>0. Uniqueness of the zero is not needed, so the theorem is stronger than the manuscript statement.

Steps: D2

Lean declaration and proof
theorem residual_distance {f : ℝ→ℝ} {a b x z m : ℝ}
    (hx : x∈Icc a b) (hz : z∈Icc a b) (hzero : f z=0)
    (hm : 0<m) (hc : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b))
    (hd : ∀t∈Ioo a b,DifferentiableAt ℝ f t)
    (hl : ∀t∈Ioo a b,m≤|deriv f t|) :
    |x-z|≤|f x|/m := by
  apply (le_div_iff₀ hm).mpr
  rcases lt_trichotomy x z with h|h|h
  · have hi : Icc x z⊆Icc a b:=fun t ht=>⟨hx.1.trans ht.1,ht.2.trans hz.2⟩
    have hj : Ioo x z⊆Ioo a b:=fun t ht=>⟨lt_of_le_of_lt hx.1 ht.1,lt_of_lt_of_le ht.2 hz.2⟩
    have hv:=mean_value_lower_bound h (hc.mono hi)
      (fun t ht=>hd t (hj ht)) (fun t ht=>hl t (hj ht))
    rw [hzero,zero_sub,abs_neg] at hv
    rw [abs_of_neg (sub_neg.mpr h)]
    nlinarith only [hv]
  · subst z; simp

lemma factor_ranges {rho : ℝ} (hr : rho ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1) :
    let rh := round rho
    let a := round (1-rh)
    let b := round (1+rh)
    let v := round (round (a/2)/b)
    let r := round (1-v)
    let k := round (r*r)
    rh ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ a ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 ∧
    b ∈ Set.Icc (1:ℝ) 2 ∧ v ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) (1/2) ∧
    r ∈ Set.Icc (1/2:ℝ) 1 ∧ k ∈ Set.Icc (1/4:ℝ) 1 := by
  dsimp only
  have hrh := round_interval round_zero round_one hr
  have ha := round_interval round_zero round_one
    (show 1-round rho ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 by constructor <;> linarith [hrh.1, hrh.2])
  have hb := round_interval round_one round_two
    (show 1+round rho ∈ Set.Icc (1:ℝ) 2 by constructor <;> linarith [hrh.1, hrh.2])
  have hbpos : 0 < round (1+round rho) := by linarith [hb.1]
  have hvarg : round (round (1-round rho)/2)/round (1+round rho) ∈
      Set.Icc (0:ℝ) (1/2) := by
    rw [factor_halving_exact hr]
    constructor
    · exact div_nonneg (by linarith [ha.1]) (le_of_lt hbpos)
    · apply (div_le_iff₀ hbpos).mpr
      linarith [ha.2, hb.1]
  have hv := round_interval round_zero round_half hvarg
  have hrarg : 1-round (round (round (1-round rho)/2)/round (1+round rho)) ∈
      Set.Icc (1/2:ℝ) 1 := by constructor <;> linarith [hv.1, hv.2]
  have hrr := round_interval round_half round_one hrarg
  have hkarg : round (1-round (round (round (1-round rho)/2)/round (1+round rho))) *
      round (1-round (round (round (1-round rho)/2)/round (1+round rho))) ∈
      Set.Icc (1/4:ℝ) 1 := by constructor <;> nlinarith [hrr.1, hrr.2]
  exact ⟨hrh, ha, hb, hv, hrr, round_interval round_quarter round_one hkarg⟩

def factorTrace (rho : ℝ) (hr : rho ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1) :
    FactorTrace binary64Epsilon rho := by
  let rh := round rho
  let a := round (1-rh)
  let b := round (1+rh)
  let v := round (round (a/2)/b)
  let r := round (1-v)
  let k := round (r*r)
  have ranges := factor_ranges hr
  change rh ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ a ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 ∧
    b ∈ Set.Icc (1:ℝ) 2 ∧ v ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) (1/2) ∧
    r ∈ Set.Icc (1/2:ℝ) 1 ∧ k ∈ Set.Icc (1/4:ℝ) 1 at ranges
  have hrh := ranges.1
  have ha := ranges.2.1
  have hb := ranges.2.2.1
  have hv := ranges.2.2.2.1
  have hrr := ranges.2.2.2.2.1
  have hk := ranges.2.2.2.2.2
  have half : round (a/2) = a/2 := factor_halving_exact hr
  have hquot : (a/2)/b ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) (1/2) := by
    have bp : 0 < b := by linarith [hb.1]
    constructor
    · exact div_nonneg (by linarith [ha.1]) (le_of_lt bp)
    · apply (div_le_iff₀ bp).mpr; linarith [ha.2, hb.1]
  refine {
    rhoHat := rh, aHat := a, bHat := b, vHat := v, rHat := r, kHat := k

    r_range := hrr, k_range := hk
    rho_error := round_error (abs_le_two_of_unit hr)
    a_error := ?_, b_error := ?_, v_error := ?_, r_error := ?_, k_error := ?_ }

  · apply round_error; apply abs_le.mpr; constructor <;> linarith [hrh.1, hrh.2]
  · dsimp only [v]; rw [half]; exact round_error (abs_le_two_of_half hquot)
  · apply round_error; apply abs_le.mpr; constructor <;> linarith [hv.1, hv.2]
  · change Within (round (r*r)) (r^2) _

def scaledTrace (rho p1 p2 p3 : ℝ) (hr : rho ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1)
    (h1 : |p1| ≤ 1) (h2 : |p2| ≤ 1) (h3 : |p3| ≤ 1)
    (hs : (p1 ≤ 0 ∧ 0 ≤ p2) ∨ (p2 ≤ 0 ∧ 0 ≤ p1)) :
    ScaledTrace binary64Epsilon rho p1 p2 p3 := by
  let ft := factorTrace rho hr
  let q1 := round p1
  let q2 := round p2
  let q3 := round p3
  let s := round (q1+q2)
  let h := round (s/2)
  let d := round (q3-h)
  let u := round (ft.kHat*|h|)
  let v := round (ft.kHat*|q3|)
  let w := round (u+v)
  let g := round (w-|d|)
  have hq1 : |q1| ≤ 1 := round_abs_le_one h1
  have hq2 : |q2| ≤ 1 := round_abs_le_one h2
  have hq3 : |q3| ≤ 1 := round_abs_le_one h3
  have hsarg : |q1+q2| ≤ 1 := opposite_sum_bound hq1 hq2 (round_signs hs)
  have hsum : |s| ≤ 1 := round_abs_le_one hsarg
  have hharg : |s/2| ≤ 1/2 := by rw [abs_div]; norm_num; linarith
  have hh : |h| ≤ 1/2 := abs_le.mpr
    (round_interval round_neg_half round_half (abs_le.mp hharg))
  have hdarg : |q3-h| ≤ 2 := by
    rcases abs_le.mp hq3 with ⟨hl,hu⟩
    rcases abs_le.mp hh with ⟨hl',hu'⟩
    apply abs_le.mpr; constructor <;> linarith
  have hd : |d| ≤ 2 := round_abs_le_two hdarg
  have hk := ft.k_range
  have huarg : ft.kHat*|h| ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) (1/2) := by
    constructor
    · exact mul_nonneg (by linarith [hk.1]) (abs_nonneg _)
    · nlinarith [hk.1, hk.2, abs_nonneg h]
  have hvarg : ft.kHat*|q3| ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 := by
    constructor
    · exact mul_nonneg (by linarith [hk.1]) (abs_nonneg _)
    · nlinarith [hk.1, hk.2, abs_nonneg q3]
  have hu : u ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) (1/2) := round_interval round_zero round_half huarg
  have hv : v ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 := round_interval round_zero round_one hvarg
  have hwarg : u+v ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 2 := by constructor <;> linarith [hu.1,hu.2,hv.1,hv.2]
  have hw : w ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 2 := round_interval round_zero round_two hwarg
  have hgarg : |w - abs d| ≤ 2 := by
    apply abs_le.mpr; constructor <;> linarith [hw.1, hw.2, abs_nonneg d]
  refine {
    factor := ft, p1Hat := q1, p2Hat := q2, p3Hat := q3
    sumHat := s, hHat := h, diffHat := d, productH := u, productP := v
    rightHat := w, gapHat := g
    p1_range := hq1, p2_range := hq2, p3_range := hq3, sum_range := hsum, h_range := hh
    p1_error := round_error (by linarith), p2_error := round_error (by linarith)
    p3_error := round_error (by linarith), sum_error := round_error (by linarith)
    h_error := round_error (by linarith), diff_error := round_error hdarg
    productH_error := round_error (abs_le_two_of_half huarg)
    productP_error := round_error (abs_le_two_of_unit hvarg)
    right_error := round_error (by rw [abs_of_nonneg hwarg.1]; exact hwarg.2)
    gap_error := round_error hgarg }

  | initial : History B M W0 0 W0 .bisection

theorem history_decomposes {B W0 w : ℝ} {M n : ℕ} {mode : Mode}
    (h : History B M W0 n w mode) : Decomposed B M W0 n w mode := by
  induction h with
  | initial => exact .ready .initial
  | bisectStay old ih =>
      cases ih with
      | ready hp => exact .ready (.bisect hp)
      | stopped hp ha hw hmono =>
          simpa only [Nat.add_assoc] using Decomposed.ready (CompletedPrefix.phase hp ha hw hmono)
  | bisectStart old ih =>
      cases ih with
      | ready hp => simpa using Decomposed.active (CompletedPrefix.bisect hp) ActivePhase.start
      | stopped hp ha hw hmono =>
          simpa only [Nat.add_zero,Nat.add_assoc] using
            Decomposed.active (CompletedPrefix.phase hp ha hw hmono) ActivePhase.start
  | abWidth old hw hmono ht ih =>
      cases ih with
      | active hp ha =>
          simpa only [Nat.add_assoc] using Decomposed.active hp (ActivePhase.width ha hw hmono ht)
  | abException old hw hmono ht hc ih =>
      cases ih with
      | active hp ha =>
          simpa only [Nat.add_assoc] using Decomposed.active hp (ActivePhase.exception ha hw hmono ht hc)
  | abStop old hw hmono ih =>
      cases ih with
      | active hp ha => exact .stopped hp ha hw hmono

theorem history_credits {B W0 w : ℝ} {M n d : ℕ} {mode : Mode}
    (hB : (1/2:ℝ)≤B) (hW0 : 0≤W0) (hC : envelopeConstant B M≤(2:ℝ)^d)
    (h : History B M W0 n w mode) :
    ∃ H : ℕ, w≤W0/(2:ℝ)^H ∧ n≤(d+2)*H+(d+1) := by
  have hd:=history_decomposes h
  cases hd with
  | ready hp =>
      obtain ⟨H,hw,hn⟩:=prefix_credits hB hW0 hC hp
      exact ⟨H,hw,by omega⟩
  | @active n S t c w hp ha =>
      obtain ⟨H,hw,hn⟩:=prefix_credits hB hW0 hC hp
      obtain ⟨k,hk,ht⟩:=tail_bound hB (prefix_nonnegative hW0 hp) hC (Tail.active ha)
      refine ⟨H+k,?_,?_⟩
      · exact hk.trans ((div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hw (by positivity : 0≤(2:ℝ)^k)).trans_eq
          (dyadic_compose W0 H k))
      · nlinarith
  | @stopped n S t c u w hp ha hw0 hmono =>
      obtain ⟨H,hw,hn⟩:=prefix_credits hB hW0 hC hp
      obtain ⟨k,hk,ht⟩:=tail_bound hB (prefix_nonnegative hW0 hp) hC (Tail.stopped ha hw0 hmono)
      refine ⟨H+k,?_,?_⟩
      · exact hk.trans ((div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hw (by positivity : 0≤(2:ℝ)^k)).trans_eq
          (dyadic_compose W0 H k))
      · nlinarith

theorem input_facts (env : Nat → ℝ) (hd : Domain env) :
    0 < scale env ∧ rho env ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 ∧
    |normalized env 0| ≤ 1 ∧ |normalized env 1| ≤ 1 ∧ |normalized env 2| ≤ 1 ∧
    ((normalized env 0 ≤ 0 ∧ 0 ≤ normalized env 1) ∨
      (normalized env 1 ≤ 0 ∧ 0 ≤ normalized env 0)) := by
  have h0 : 0 < |env 0| := abs_pos.mpr hd.1
  have h1 : 0 < |env 1| := abs_pos.mpr hd.2.1
  have hp : 0 < scale env := lt_of_lt_of_le h0
    ((le_max_left _ _).trans (le_max_left _ _))
  have hb (i : Nat) (hi : |env i| ≤ scale env) : |normalized env i| ≤ 1 := by
    dsimp [normalized]
    rw [abs_div, abs_of_pos hp]
    exact (div_le_one hp).mpr hi
  refine ⟨hp, endpoint_rho_range h0 h1,
    hb 0 ((le_max_left _ _).trans (le_max_left _ _)),
    hb 1 ((le_max_right _ _).trans (le_max_left _ _)), hb 2 (le_max_right _ _), ?_⟩
  rcases hd.2.2 with ⟨ha,hb⟩ | ⟨ha,hb⟩
  · exact Or.inl ⟨div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg ha hp.le, div_nonneg hb hp.le⟩
  · exact Or.inr ⟨div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg ha hp.le, div_nonneg hb hp.le⟩

theorem source_safe (env : Nat → ℝ) (hd : Domain env) : gapExpr.Safe env := by
  let t := trace env hd
  obtain ⟨hscale, hrho, hp1, hp2, hp3, hsign⟩ := input_facts env hd
  have srho : rhoExpr.Safe env := by
    refine ⟨⟨True.intro,True.intro⟩, ⟨True.intro,True.intro⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact abs_le_two_of_unit hrho

lemma product_error {x x' y y' A B C D : ℝ}
    (hx : |x'| ≤ A) (hy : Within y' y B)
    (hd : Within x' x C) (hb : |y| ≤ D) :
    Within (x'*y') (x*y) (A*B+C*D) := by
  have hA : 0 ≤ A := le_trans (abs_nonneg _) hx
  have hC : 0 ≤ C := le_trans (abs_nonneg _) hd
  calc
    |x'*y' - x*y| = |x'*(y'-y)+(x'-x)*y| := by congr 1; ring
    _ ≤ |x'*(y'-y)| + |(x'-x)*y| := abs_add_le _ _
    _ = |x'| *|y'-y| + |x'-x| *|y| := by rw [abs_mul, abs_mul]
    _ ≤ A*B+C*D := add_le_add
      (mul_le_mul hx hy (abs_nonneg _) hA)
      (mul_le_mul hd hb (abs_nonneg _) hC)

lemma · ModAB/Switching.lean:125–141

thm:formal_switching

Factor κ(x)−κ(y)=(x−y)c, prove 0≤c≤1, and take absolute values. This is the separate algebraic argument in the manuscript’s machine-formalization section.

Steps: F5

Lean declaration and proof
lemma kappa_lipschitz_algebraic {x y : ℝ} (hx : 0≤x) (hy : 0≤y) :
    |kappa x-kappa y|≤|x-y| := by
  let d:=(1+x)^2*(1+y)^2
  let c:=(1+2*x+2*y+3*x*y)/d
  have hd : 0<d:=by dsimp [d]; positivity
  have hc0 : 0≤c:=by dsimp [c]; positivity
  have hc1 : c≤1:=by
    apply (div_le_iff₀ hd).mpr
    dsimp [d]
    have hp : 0≤x*y+x^2+y^2+2*x^2*y+2*x*y^2+x^2*y^2:=by positivity
    nlinarith only [hp]
  have hid : kappa x-kappa y=(x-y)*c:=by
    dsimp [kappa,c,d]
    field_simp
    ring
  rw [hid,abs_mul,abs_of_nonneg hc0]
  nlinarith [abs_nonneg (x-y)]

    (1-r)/(2*(1+r)) ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) (1/2) := by

  · apply div_nonneg <;> linarith [hr.1, hr.2]
  · apply (div_le_iff₀ hd).mpr

lemma · ModAB/Switching.lean:151–179

thm:switch_scaled_error

Splits the numerator and denominator contributions; each is at most e/2, giving e.

Steps: S4

Lean declaration and proof
lemma quotient_error {a A b B e : ℝ} (he : 0 ≤ e)
    (ha : a ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hB : 1 ≤ B)
    (hae : Within A a e) (hbe : Within B b e) :
    Within ((A/2)/B) (a/(2*b)) e := by
  change |A-a| ≤ e at hae
  have bp : 0 < b := by linarith
  have Bp : 0 < B := by linarith
  have h₁ : Within (A/(2*B)) (a/(2*B)) (e/2) := by
    unfold Within
    rw [← sub_div, abs_div, abs_of_pos (by positivity : 0 < 2*B)]
    apply (div_le_iff₀ (by positivity : 0 < 2*B)).mpr
    have hp := mul_nonneg he (sub_nonneg.mpr hB)
    nlinarith [hae]
  have h₂ : Within (a/(2*B)) (a/(2*b)) (e/2) := by
    have hid : a/(2*B)-a/(2*b) = a*(b-B)/(2*B*b) := by field_simp
    unfold Within
    rw [hid, abs_div, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg ha.1,
      abs_of_pos (by positivity : 0 < 2*B*b)]
    apply (div_le_iff₀ (by positivity : 0 < 2*B*b)).mpr
    have hab : |b-B| ≤ e := by simpa [Within, abs_sub_comm] using hbe
    have hm : a*|b-B| ≤ e := by
      calc
        a*|b-B| ≤ 1*e := mul_le_mul ha.2 hab (abs_nonneg _) (by norm_num)
        _ = e := one_mul e
    have hprod : 1 ≤ B*b := by nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hB) (sub_nonneg.mpr hb)]
    have hep := mul_nonneg he (sub_nonneg.mpr hprod)
    nlinarith
  have h := within_trans h₁ h₂
  convert h using 1 <;> ring

  r_range : rHat ∈ Set.Icc (1/2:ℝ) 1
  k_range : kHat ∈ Set.Icc (1/4:ℝ) 1
  rho_error : Within rhoHat rho e
  a_error : Within aHat (1-rhoHat) e
  b_error : Within bHat (1+rhoHat) e
  v_error : Within vHat ((aHat/2)/bHat) e
  r_error : Within rHat (1-vHat) e

theorem · ModAB/Switching.lean:199–223

thm:switch_scaled_error, thm:formal_switching

Common quotient, subtraction, and square-error chain e→2e→3e→7e→8e. The caller must prove the κ perturbation bound; it is supplied by the corresponding mean-value or algebraic lemma.

Steps: S4, S5, F5

Lean declaration and proof
theorem factor_error_from_coefficient {e rho : ℝ} (he : 0≤e)
    (t : FactorTrace e rho) (hp : Within (kappa t.rhoHat) (kappa rho) e) :
    Within t.kHat (kappa rho) (8*e) := by
  let v₀ := (1-t.rhoHat)/(2*(1+t.rhoHat))
  have hv₀ := ratio_range t.rho_range
  have hq := quotient_error he
    (a := 1-t.rhoHat) (A := t.aHat) (b := 1+t.rhoHat) (B := t.bHat)
    (by constructor <;> linarith [t.rho_range.1, t.rho_range.2])
    (by linarith [t.rho_range.1]) t.b_range.1 t.a_error t.b_error
  have hv : Within t.vHat v₀ (2*e) := by
    simpa [v₀, two_mul] using within_trans t.v_error hq
  have hr : Within t.rHat (1-v₀) (3*e) := by
    have hs := within_sub (within_refl (1:ℝ)) hv
    have ht := within_trans t.r_error hs
    convert ht using 1 ; ring
  have hs := square_error
    (x := t.rHat) (y := 1-v₀)
    (by constructor <;> linarith [t.r_range.1, t.r_range.2])
    (by constructor <;> dsimp [v₀] <;> linarith [hv₀.1, hv₀.2]) hr
  have hk : Within t.kHat (kappa t.rhoHat) (7*e) := by
    rw [kappa_identity t.rho_range.1]
    have ht := within_trans t.k_error hs
    convert ht using 1 ; ring
  have ht := within_trans hk hp
  convert ht using 1 ; ring

theorem · ModAB/Switching.lean:267–300

thm:switch_scaled_error, thm:formal_switching

Common remaining estimates given the proved coefficient error: midpoint 3e, left side 5e, product with p₃ at 10e before product with h at 8e, right side 19e, and rounded gap 25e. The product order now follows the manuscript.

Steps: S6, S7, S8, S9, F5

Lean declaration and proof
theorem scaled_errors_from_factor {e rho p1 p2 p3 : ℝ} (he : 0 ≤ e)
    (hh : |exactH p1 p2| ≤ 1/2) (hp3 : |p3| ≤ 1)
    (t : ScaledTrace e rho p1 p2 p3) (hk : Within t.factor.kHat (kappa rho) (8*e)) :
    Within t.factor.kHat (kappa rho) (8*e) ∧
    Within t.hHat (exactH p1 p2) (3*e) ∧
    Within |t.diffHat| (exactL p1 p2 p3) (5*e) ∧
    Within t.rightHat (exactR rho p1 p2 p3) (19*e) ∧
    Within t.gapHat (exactG rho p1 p2 p3) (25*e) := by
  have hsum := within_trans t.sum_error (within_add t.p1_error t.p2_error)
  have hmid := within_trans t.h_error (within_half hsum)
  have hm : Within t.hHat (exactH p1 p2) (3*e) := by
    exact within_mono hmid (by linarith)
  have hl₀ := within_trans t.diff_error (within_sub t.p3_error hm)
  have hl : Within |t.diffHat| (exactL p1 p2 p3) (5*e) := by
    have ha := within_abs hl₀
    convert ha using 1 <;> (try dsimp [exactL]) <;> ring
  have hkb : |t.factor.kHat| ≤ 1 := by
    rw [abs_of_nonneg (by linarith [t.factor.k_range.1] : 0 ≤ t.factor.kHat)]
    exact t.factor.k_range.2
  have pp₀ := product_error hkb (within_abs t.p3_error) hk (by simpa using hp3)
  have pp : Within t.productP (kappa rho*|p3|) (10*e) := by
    have ha := within_trans t.productP_error pp₀
    convert ha using 1 ; ring
  have ph₀ := product_error hkb (within_abs hm) hk (by simpa using hh)
  have ph : Within t.productH (kappa rho*|exactH p1 p2|) (8*e) := by
    have ha := within_trans t.productH_error ph₀
    convert ha using 1 ; ring
  have hright : Within t.rightHat (exactR rho p1 p2 p3) (19*e) := by
    have ha := within_trans t.right_error (within_add ph pp)
    convert ha using 1 <;> (try dsimp [exactR]) <;> ring
  have hgap : Within t.gapHat (exactG rho p1 p2 p3) (25*e) := by
    have ha := within_trans t.gap_error (within_sub hright hl)
    convert ha using 1 <;> (try dsimp [exactG]) <;> ring
  exact ⟨hk, hm, hl, hright, hgap⟩

def evaluate (f1 f2 f3 : ℝ) : Values :=
  let su := Binary64.round (f1+f2)
  let di := Binary64.round (f2-f1)
  let y := Binary64.round (su/2)
  let v := Binary64.round (|y|/|di|)

  let k := Binary64.round (r*r)
  let leftDiff := Binary64.round (f3-y)
  let py := Binary64.round (k*|y|)
  let pz := Binary64.round (k*|f3|)

theorem factor_ranges {f1 f2 f3 : ℝ} (hs : f1*f2<0) (hn : NormalRun f1 f2 f3) :
    let t:=evaluate f1 f2 f3
    0≤t.v ∧ t.v<1 ∧ t.r∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ t.k∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 := by
  let t:=evaluate f1 f2 f3
  have hv0 : 0≤t.v := by
    change 0 ≤ Binary64.round (|t.y|/|t.diff|)
    have h := round_monotone (show (0:ℝ)≤|t.y|/|t.diff| by positivity)
    simpa only [Binary64.round_zero] using h
  have hv := quotient_error hs hn
  have vr := Cubic.ratio_range hs
  have hvl := (abs_le.mp hv).2
  have hv1 : t.v<1 := by
    have hgam := eps_bounds.2.2.2
    have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left vr.2 hgam.1.le
    change t.v- (|(f1+f2)/2|/|f2-f1|) ≤ _ at hvl
    nlinarith
  have hr : t.r∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 := by
    change Binary64.round (1-t.v)∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1
    exact round_interval Binary64.round_zero Binary64.round_one
      (show 1-t.v∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 by constructor <;> linarith)
  have hk : t.k∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 := by
    change Binary64.round (t.r*t.r)∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1
    exact round_interval Binary64.round_zero Binary64.round_one
      (show t.r*t.r∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 by constructor <;> nlinarith [hr.1,hr.2])
  exact ⟨hv0,hv1,hr,hk⟩

Lean declaration and proof
theorem factor_error {f1 f2 f3 : ℝ} (hs : f1*f2<0) (hn : NormalRun f1 f2 f3) :
    Within (evaluate f1 f2 f3).k ((1-|(f1+f2)/2|/|f2-f1|)^2) (2*gamma 3) := by
  let t:=evaluate f1 f2 f3
  let v:=|(f1+f2)/2|/|f2-f1|
  obtain ⟨d,hd,hr⟩ := rounded_relative hn.subtract
  obtain ⟨c,hc,hk⟩ := rounded_relative hn.square
  have hmodel : t.k=(1-t.v)^2*((1+d)*(1+d)*(1+c)) := by
    change t.r=(1-t.v)*(1+d) at hr
    change t.k=(t.r*t.r)*(1+c) at hk
    rw [hk,hr]; ring
  have tr := factor_ranges hs hn
  have vr := Cubic.ratio_range hs
  have hh : 0≤(1-t.v)^2 ∧ (1-t.v)^2≤1 := by
    constructor
    · positivity
    · nlinarith [tr.1,tr.2.1]
  have hlocal : Within t.k ((1-t.v)^2) (gamma 3) := by
    unfold Within
    rw [hmodel]
    have hid : (1-t.v)^2*((1+d)*(1+d)*(1+c))-(1-t.v)^2 =
        (1-t.v)^2*((1+d)*(1+d)*(1+c)-1) := by ring
    rw [hid,abs_mul,abs_of_nonneg hh.1]
    have hg := factor_three_gamma hd hd hc
    have hm := mul_le_mul hh.2 hg (abs_nonneg _) (by norm_num : (0:ℝ)≤1)
    simpa using hm
  have hq := quotient_error hs hn
  have hrerr := within_sub (within_refl (1:ℝ)) hq
  have hsquare := square_error
    (x:=1-t.v) (y:=1-v)
    (by constructor <;> linarith [tr.1,tr.2.1])
    (by constructor <;> dsimp [v] <;> linarith [vr.1,vr.2]) hrerr
  have h := within_trans hlocal hsquare
  apply within_mono h
  have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left vr.2 (le_of_lt eps_bounds.2.2.2.1)
  dsimp [v] at *
  linarith

theorem distributed_error {a b A B R : ℝ} (ha : 0≤a) (hb : 0≤b)
    (hA : Relative A a) (hB : Relative B b) (hR : Relative R (A+B)) :
    Within R (a+b) (gamma 2*(a+b)) := by
  obtain ⟨d,hd,rfl⟩ := hA
  obtain ⟨e,he,rfl⟩ := hB
  obtain ⟨c,hc,rfl⟩ := hR
  unfold Within
  have hid : (a*(1+d)+b*(1+e))*(1+c)-(a+b)=
      a*((1+d)*(1+c)-1)+b*((1+e)*(1+c)-1) := by ring
  rw [hid]
  calc
    |a*((1+d)*(1+c)-1)+b*((1+e)*(1+c)-1)| ≤
      |a*((1+d)*(1+c)-1)|+|b*((1+e)*(1+c)-1)| := abs_add_le _ _
    _ = a*|(1+d)*(1+c)-1|+b*|(1+e)*(1+c)-1| := by
      rw [abs_mul,abs_mul,abs_of_nonneg ha,abs_of_nonneg hb]
    _ ≤ a*gamma 2+b*gamma 2 := add_le_add
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (factor_two_gamma hd hc) ha)
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (factor_two_gamma he hc) hb)
    _ = gamma 2*(a+b) := by ring
